## How status is decided

A workflow is **built** when and only when its feature module is on
`origin/main`. That is the same test the plugin host applies — a module
that exists only in a branch is a claim to verify, not a feature. Nothing
here is copied from another status file, because a derived number cached
anywhere else is a number that goes stale.

Criticality is the judgment in
`docs/research/digital-sales-room-workflows/criticality-decisions.json`:
**critical** means removing it leaves no usable sales room;
**supplementary** means the primary loop still closes without it.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ✅ Built | Feature module on `origin/main`, reachable over HTTP |
| ⬜ Pending — critical | Specified and judged critical; no code yet |
| ⬜ Pending — supplementary | Specified; primary loop closes without it |

## Provenance

| Source | What it contributes |
|---|---|
| `origin/main` | built/pending, measured from the feature registry |
| `criticality-decisions.json` | the criticality judgment and its basis |
| `wf/WF-*.md` | each workflow's name and whether its spec is complete |
| `catalogue.json` | the deduped count |

No new source of truth is introduced: built-state is never stored in a
file, only measured. If the host learns a feature this board does not
list, that is the bug — regenerate and the two agree.

A spec marked **incomplete** is missing one of the sections the corpus
requires. It is still buildable, but the brief would be working from a
 thinner document than the rest.
